prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car-accident case — the right lawyer depends on your injuries, insurance situation, whether the case will likely settle or go to trial, and your communication/style preferences. I can help you find the best match. A quick guide and next steps:

Quick questions so I can narrow recommendations
- What Chicago neighborhood or ZIP code are you in (so I can find local attorneys)?
- How serious are your injuries (minor, moderate, severe, catastrophic)?
- Was the other driver uninsured or underinsured, or was liability disputed?
- Do you prefer a large firm with lots of resources or a smaller boutique trial lawyer?
- Any language needs or budget concerns?

What to look for when choosing an attorney
- Experience with car-accident/auto-injury cases (not just general practice).
- Trial experience and successful verdicts/settlements for cases like yours.
- Clear contingency-fee agreement (most PI lawyers work on contingency).
- Good client communication: timely responses and regular updates.
- Reputation: peer reviews, client reviews, and disciplinary record.
- Resources to handle medical records, expert witnesses, and litigation.

How to vet candidates quickly
- Ask for examples of similar cases and outcomes.
- Ask whether they handle cases personally or assign them to junior lawyers.
- Confirm contingency fee % and who pays litigation expenses.
- Read recent client reviews and check ISBA/Chicago Bar records.
- Get a free initial consultation (most PI attorneys offer one).

Some well-known Chicago personal injury firms (examples to consider)
- Clifford Law Offices
- Corboy & Demetrio
- Salvi, Schostok & Pateur
- Levin & Perconti
- Simmons Hanly Conroy
- Power Rogers & Smith

(These are examples of established Chicago firms; I’m not saying any single one is the best for your specific case.)

Immediate practical steps
1) Preserve evidence: photos of the vehicles/scenes, medical records, police report, witness info.
2) Don’t give recorded statements to the insurer before talking to a lawyer.
3) Set up 2–3 free consultations and compare answers to the vetting questions above.

If you want, tell me your ZIP code and a bit about your injuries/insurance situation and I’ll:
- Pull together a short list (3–5) of attorneys near you who handle car-accident claims, with notes on their strengths, typical fee structure, and contact info.
- Or draft a short script/email you can use when contacting attorneys for initial consultations.
